subject: Information Theory
title: Copyright and Information Sharing
description: A quick win: understand Copyright and Information Sharing.

hook.text: A pop song is 3 minutes of audio—about 30 megabytes. Copyright protects those 30 MB for 70 years after the creator dies.

buildup.text: Copyright restricts copying: the core operation of information systems. It limits who can duplicate a bit arrangement.

discovery.text: The economic logic: without protection, creators can't recover creation costs because copying is nearly free.

twist.text: Digital copying costs effectively zero. Copyright law fights the physics of information—bits want to replicate.

climax.text: The tension: information theory says copying is the cheapest operation. Copyright law says it's the most restricted.

punchline.text: Bits copy for free. Law says they can't. The tension never resolves.

quiz.question: Why is copyright enforcement harder in the digital age?
options: Digital copying is nearly free, fighting the natural physics of information
